get.summary: Page through the template set, configured templates included
get.description: Returns one page of every template the registry holds, configured ones included, ordered by template name. A page holds 50 entries when the request names no limit; a limit of 0 reads the same way, and a limit above 200 is capped at 200. The decision is made in the platform domain on sms.template.read, so a grant in a tenant does not reach this set.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Continue after the template this name names

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page's maximum size; the read surface caps it

200.description: One page of templates, ordered by name, and the cursor of the next, empty on the last page

schema.description: One page of the template set, ordered by name, with the cursor that continues it.

templates.description: The templates on this page, ordered by name.

next_cursor.description: The last name on this page, to be passed as after on the next request; empty when this page is the last.

400.description: The limit is not a non-negative integer

403.description: The caller holds no sms.template.read in the platform domain

post.summary: Take up a template whose vendor code the operator already has
post.description: Takes up a runtime template whose vendor code the operator already has. Every language named starts pending and the template starts enabled: enablement is independent of the vendor's review, which the registry reads back per language from then on. A name that is empty or only whitespace is a 400 before the registry is called, and a language the name already holds is a 409. The mandatory audit row is written before the action and outside any transaction, so an audit failure answers 503 and takes nothing up.

requestBody.description: The template to take up: its logical name, the parameter names it substitutes in order, and the vendor code for each language.

400.description: The name is empty, the body is not one object, or the template set is one the registry cannot run on

403.description: The caller holds no sms.template.manage in the platform domain

409.description: The registry already holds the name

post.summary: Hand a template to the vendor for review and take up the code it answers with
post.description: Hands a template to the vendor for review through the vendor's own API and takes up the code the vendor answers with; the submission's language starts pending. Content is written with ${name} placeholders naming the entries of params, and a carrier whose vendor takes positional placeholders rewrites them in params order. An empty or whitespace-only name is a 400 before the vendor is called; a submission the vendor or the registry refuses is a 400, and a language the name already holds is a 409. The mandatory audit row is written before the action and outside any transaction, so an audit failure answers 503 and submits nothing.

requestBody.description: The template to submit: its logical name, the body with ${name} placeholders, what the template is for, its language, the parameter names in order, and a note for the reviewer.

template.description: The created template, with its language starting pending review.

400.description: The name is empty, the body is not one object, or the vendor or the registry refused the submission

403.description: The caller holds no sms.template.manage in the platform domain

409.description: The registry already holds the name

delete.summary: Drop a runtime template from this process, the vendor left alone
delete.description: Drops a runtime template from this process; the vendor's copy is left alone. A template that came from the configuration cannot be removed at runtime: naming one is a 409 whose problem type is urn:speed:sms:config-template, while a name the registry does not hold is a 404 with no problem body. The mandatory audit row is written before the action and outside any transaction, so an audit failure answers 503 and removes nothing. Success is 204 with no body.

parameters.description: The logical template name, the natural key the management routes address a template by.

403.description: The caller holds no sms.template.manage in the platform domain

404.description: The registry holds no template by the name

409.description: The template came from the configuration and is immutable at runtime

post.summary: Turn a runtime template's ability to send on or off
post.description: Turns a runtime template's ability to send on or off. Enablement is orthogonal to the vendor's review: a template may be enabled while its review is still pending, and a send still waits for the review. The body must carry enabled; a body without it is a 400 rather than a disable by omission. A configured template is a 409 whose problem type is urn:speed:sms:config-template, and an unknown name is a 404. The mandatory audit row is written before the action and outside any transaction, so an audit failure answers 503 and changes nothing. Success is 204 with no body.

parameters.description: The logical template name, the natural key the management routes address a template by.

requestBody.description: The state to set on the template.

schema.description: The target state of the template's ability to send.

enabled.description: True lets messages go out under the template, false stops them. The member is required and must be a JSON boolean; a body without it is a 400.

400.description: The body names no state, or is not one object

403.description: The caller holds no sms.template.manage in the platform domain

404.description: The registry holds no template by the name

409.description: The template came from the configuration and is immutable at runtime

SmsAdminName.name: name
SmsAdminName.description: The logical template name, the natural key the management routes address a template by.

SmsAdminTemplate.description: One template as the management surface reports it: its logical name, its source, its ordered parameter names, the languages it holds a code for, the vendor's review per language, whether sends are allowed, and its write counters. It carries no vendor code.

name.description: The logical template name a caller sends under; the management routes address a template by it.

source.description: Where the template came from: config for one read from the configuration, runtime for one this process created. A config template is read-only at runtime, always enabled, and carries no approvals and no version.

params.description: The parameter names the template substitutes, in the order the vendor approved them; a positional vendor lays values out in this order.

locales.description: The languages the template holds a vendor code for. A code is what a send needs but not the whole of what it needs: a runtime template sends only while it is enabled and the language's vendor review is approved, and every language a runtime template names starts pending review whether the template was registered or submitted, so this list normally includes languages that cannot be sent in yet. A configured template is always enabled and its review is not tracked, so each language it holds a code for can be sent in.

approvals.description: The vendor's review verdict per language, keyed by locale; a vendor approves a template per language. A configured template carries an empty object because this process does not track its review.

enabled.description: Whether a message may go out under the template. A configured template is always enabled; a runtime template's value is set by the enable route and is independent of the vendor's review.

version.description: The number of writes this runtime record has taken, used as the optimistic-concurrency condition; 0 for a configured template, which has no version.

created_at.description: When the record was first written, in UTC and RFC 3339 format; the zero time for a configured template.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written, in UTC and RFC 3339 format; the zero time for a configured template.

SmsAdminApproval.description: The vendor's review verdict on one template in one language.

state.description: The verdict in this capability's own vocabulary: pending, approved, rejected or withdrawn; an empty string means a review this process does not track. The vendor's raw status numbers are never exposed.

reason.description: The vendor's own explanation, present when it turned the template down and it gave one; omitted otherwise.

SmsAdminRegister.description: The body of a registration: a template whose vendor code the operator already has.

name.description: The logical template name to take up; required and non-empty, and the name a caller will later send under. A language the name already holds is a 409.

params.description: The parameter names the template substitutes, in the order the vendor approved them.

codes.description: The vendor's template code per language, keyed by locale. Every language named starts pending, and the template starts enabled.

SmsAdminSubmission.description: The body of a submission: a template handed to the vendor for review.

name.description: The logical template name the submission creates; required and non-empty.

content.description: The template body, written with ${name} placeholders naming the entries of params. The carrier rewrites them into the vendor's own syntax, in params order.

kind.description: What the template is for, in the shared vocabulary: verification, notification or marketing. The carrier maps it to the vendor's spelling.

locale.description: The language this submission is for, opaque to the capability. A vendor approves per language, so one submission yields one code for one language.

params.description: The parameter names content substitutes, in the order the template expects them.

remark.description: A note for the vendor's reviewer; may be empty.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence. Present only when the answering module has one to give, and those that set one render it in the request language.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.
